summary: Sustained APAC inference p99 spike: geo-proxy sticky-session fallback causing request queueing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Brushwell Analytics reports sustained p99 inference latency increase (from ~350ms to 2.5–4s) and occasional request timeouts for requests routed to apac-east.

Impact:
- Production inference for multiple endpoints degraded for Brushwell (dedicated account).
- Client sees increased API latency and intermittent 504s; affects real-time scoring pipelines.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted, dedicated capacity for Brushwell in apac-east region.
- Observed across multiple model variants pinned to redwood-v2-medium.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Send streaming chat completion requests to customer key scoped to apac-east.
2) Observe p95/p99 token latencies and occasional streaming disconnects after 2–4s.
3) Repeatedly repros ~20% of requests during window between 2026-03-12T02:10Z and ongoing.

Observed logs / telemetry snippets:
- API gateway traces show requests routed to edge-proxy instance apac-proxy-07 then immediately retried to apac-proxy-03 with sticky cookie mismatch.
- Serving runtime shows queue depth spikes on a small subset of hosts (gpu-pool-03) concurrent with increased KV cache miss rate.
- No elevated 5xx coming from model pods; time lost in proxy handoff and connection re-establishment.

Customer-provided example request IDs:
- req_brush_20260312_00123
- req_brush_20260312_00456
comments: 2026-03-12 03:05 UTC — Ava Chen: Ticket created after customer report. Initial triage: looks like routing fallback in APAC; escalating to SRE and Edge team.

2026-03-12 04:12 UTC — Diego Morales (SRE): Captured sample traces. Noticed sticky session cookie expiry causing immediate fallback to alternate proxy; observed TCP teardown leading to request retransmit and queueing on target GPU host.

2026-03-12 07:30 UTC — Edge Team (comment): We deployed a config rollback of recent sticky-affinity change (PR 712) to a subset of apac proxies; early telemetry shows reduced immediate fallbacks but queue depth still elevated on gpu-pool-03.

2026-03-13 01:20 UTC — Diego Morales: Investigating KV cache miss patterns; hypothesis: proxy fallback mixes origin headers leading to cache key partitioning and cold KV state, increasing per-request setup time.
2026-03-14 09:10 UTC — Customer CS: Brushwell reports degradation mostly mitigated for live endpoints after temporary workaround; requesting postmortem and permanent remediation timeline.
investigation_notes:
Chronology: problem surfaced 2026-03-12. Initial traces show proxy sticky-session cookie TTL mismatch introduced by an edge config change (PR#712) made during a canary; some proxies returned Set-Cookie with shorter expiry causing clients to drop affinity and immediately fall back to alternate proxies. Fallback path triggers a connection reuse failure (TLS session not resumed) which causes short-lived TCP teardown and re-establishment. This increased head latency on a subset of GPU hosts because the request arrives without warmed KV cache and is queued behind active requests.

Findings: 
- Edge config change altered cookie domain/path TTL for apac proxies.
- Fallbacks were concentrated on gpu-pool-03 (single rack), indicating non-uniform capacity distribution and insufficient burst headroom.
- No model compute errors; root time lost in proxy handoff + KV cold starts + short TCP handshake.

Diagnostics run: 
- Collected pcap and proxy logs for samples; correlated with api-gateway traces.
- Verified PR#712 changed cookie TTL from 1h to 30s for certain routes.
- Checked autoscale metrics for gpu-pool-03: surge in queue depth (x6 baseline) and sustained CPU on proxy host.
resolution:
Mitigation applied 2026-03-12: rolled back cookie TTL change for all apac proxies and applied a temporary sticky-affinity tolerance (grace window) to prevent immediate fallback on cookie expiry. Provisioned short-term burst capacity to gpu-pool-03 and moved a subset of Brushwell traffic to neighboring GPU hosts to drain queue.

Permanent remediation plan: 
1) Revert PR#712 and add unit/regression tests for cookie TTL parity across canary groups. (Edge team) 2) Adjust routing policy to avoid concentrating fallback traffic to a single gpu pool; implement randomized fallback selection with capacity-awareness. (Routing) 3) Add monitoring alert for rapid proxy-fallback rates and queue-depth hotspots with automated temporary capacity assignment. (SRE)

Status: Customer-facing impact mitigated; workaround deployed. Follow-up tasks assigned as internal tickets INT-4281 (routing policy change) and INT-4310 (edge config test coverage). Postmortem to be published after full remediation.
next_steps:
- Complete INT-4281 and INT-4310; target completion 2026-03-21.
- Publish customer-facing postmortem and RCA by 2026-03-18.
- Monitor Brushwell SLAs for 72 hours and report telemetry to CS every 12 hours.
